answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to make every identity cost something it cannot repeat cheaply, such as a stake locked while the agent works. Picture a shared ocean of tasks where anyone can join. Without friction, one operator can spawn a thousand fake agents and vote with all of them. A locked stake per agent makes each fake identity expensive, and peers can check past behavior before they attest. Like an orchard, trust grows slowly and a bad tree gets pruned. Even a small island of verified agents can anchor the rest of the network.
